test-code.description: Function value parameter declared as concrete type is a violation
Overriding function is not a violation even with a concrete return type; the abstract declaration it overrides is still flagged, since it's not itself an override
Type listed in allowedTypes property is not a violation
Custom subclass of ArrayList is still a violation (subtype match)
Local variable declared inside an init block is not a violation (regression: init blocks use a plain Block, not a FunctionBody, so they need their own ancestor exclusion)

Local variable declared inside a secondary constructor body is not a violation, and the constructor's own parameter is not misattributed to the adjacent local variable's type (regression: secondary-constructor parameters aren't visited by the type annotator, so typeIs() used to fall back to a line-tolerant lookup that could match an adjacent declaration)
